text:
The example scripts accept only the __wrtoken refresh token. The WOLT_ACCESS_TOKEN access-token path was deliberately deleted (owner decision, 2026-09). Reason: users pasted the __wrtoken cookie into WOLT_ACCESS_TOKEN and got confusing 401s, and access tokens expire (~30 min) mid-way through order.py's long interactive flow. Do not reintroduce a second token path. SessionCredentials remains in the library for raw-header use and check_session.py.

Token handling in the examples was then reversed by the owner (2026-09). The earlier decision kept WOLT_REFRESH_TOKEN, rejected --token-file as too specific, and only printed a warning on rotation. That meant a rotated token was lost when the process exited, and the next run failed for no visible reason. browse.py and order.py now take a required --token-file and write every rotated refresh token back to it. WOLT_REFRESH_TOKEN was deleted at the same time: the owner wanted one token source, not two.

derive_checkout_fields' rules come from a 2026-09 browser HAR of a full browse-to-checkout session (smoothies venue, 68 items): assortment items NEVER carry category_id/category_ids/exclude_from_credits/exclude_from_discounts/exclude_from_discounts_min_basket (union of keys checked), yet all five browser checkout POSTs sent the exclude flags as false and category ids exactly equal to assortment categories[].item_ids membership. Hence: derive categories, default exclude flags to False, item value wins if present. The exactly-one-category restriction exists because the observed item had one category; the browser's rule for choosing the singular category_id among several is UNOBSERVED - to lift the restriction, capture a checkout of a multi-category item, don't guess. Also observed: the first checkout POST carried extra per-item keys (age_limit, is_weighted_item, venue_id) that later POSTs dropped; the server accepted both, so the plan item shape is not rigid.

Owner decision (2026-09): the library's original stance of returning only opaque delivery-target IDs was deliberately relaxed - DeliveryTarget now carries street-level display fields (alias, label_type, address, city, postcode) and PaymentMethod carries server display strings (title, subtitle), because making users cross-reference IDs in their browser defeated the tool. The boundary that remains: phone_number, user_id, coordinates, and address_form_data are deliberately NOT extracted from /v2/delivery/info, and all sensitive model fields are repr=False so logs/exceptions show only IDs. If someone proposes adding those fields or removing repr=False, that is reversing a considered decision, not an oversight.

payment-service POST /v1/payment-methods/checkout requires a 'platform' header ('Web' matches the browser) and returns HTTP 422 without it - isolated 2026-09 by live probes that replayed the browser's exact successful body and only got 200 after adding the header. The earlier hypothesis that is_ftu/is_gift_order/user_xpay_has_supported_card booleans were required was FALSIFIED by the same probes (200 without them once platform is sent); they are optional browser context. The transport now defaults platform: Web on all Wolt hosts, credential headers take precedence. If another Wolt endpoint returns an unexplained 422, compare request HEADERS against a browser HAR before touching the body.
